{{about|the cross-section of the sphere||Secant (disambiguation)}}
[[File:Ellipsoid_circular_sections.gif|thumb|199x199px|Animation showing the circular secant planes of the ellipsoid]]
A '''secant plane''' is a [[plane (geometry)|plane]] containing a nontrivial [[Cross section (geometry)|section]] of a [[sphere]] or an [[ellipsoid]], or such a plane that a sphere is projected onto. Secant planes are similar to tangent planes, which contact the sphere's surface at a point, while secant planes contact the surface along curves.

The two-dimensional representations of secant planes are [[secant line]]s, the lines that join two distinct points on a curve.

== Applications ==
{{comparison_of_cartography_surface_development.svg|300px}}
Secant planes are used in [[map projection]]s. The secant plane intersects a globe along a small circle with no distortion, forming a [[Standard parallel (map projections)|standard parallel]] which has true scale.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://geokov.com/education/map-projection.aspx|title=Map projection - types and distortion|last=|first=|website=geokov.com|access-date=2016-11-02}}</ref>
